title: Microsoft Entra strong authentication disabled
description: Detects a successful Microsoft Entra audit operation that disables strong authentication for an account.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary or unauthorized administrator may disable strong authentication to preserve access to a compromised account.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft exposes Disable Strong Authentication as a distinct audit activity, MITRE documents MFA modification as an authentication-control impairment and SigmaHQ treats the successful operation as a medium-severity signal because authorized administration remains possible.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify successful Disable Strong Authentication operations while leaving enablement, failed changes and unrelated authentication-method administration unmatched.

triage.summary: Identify the affected account and initiator, validate an approved authentication-administration request and inspect subsequent access for compromise.
steps: Review the initiating user or application, source IP, target account, correlation identifier and adjacent authentication-method events.
Confirm the change against an approved support, break-glass or identity-administration record and the expected administrator.
Inspect sign-ins, risk events, factor registrations and account changes before and after the operation; restore strong authentication and contain unauthorized access.
false_positives: Authorized identity administration, account recovery, migration or break-glass maintenance

validation.expected_outcome: Match successful strong-authentication disablement; do not match enablement, failures, unrelated method changes or missing result values.
